newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm swaps and crude push prices up.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil-Firm swaps and crude push prices up.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market continued to strengthen on the back of firm swaps quotes and crude gains as well as strong anticipation for China to re-enter the market, traders said on Monday.
Two scheduled maintenance turnarounds of two refineries in Singapore in March also fuelled concerns over possible tightening supplies, they added.
Mobil 280,000-bpd refinery will be shut down for six weeks starting March 15 and Singapore Refining Co's refinery will shut an 18,000-bpd hydrocracker unit from March 2-22.

A Chinese trader said China might soon start looking for cargoes after a long rest during the China Lunar New Year holidays in early February, but no Chinese enquiries had been heard, other traders said.
"There are more bids than offers in the bunker market, with sellers staying calm because they are waiting for prices to go further higher," said one trader on the only actively talked market.
"Talks were very thin in the cargo market today...bunker prices should not go that high," said an independent.
A major said at least three cargoes, totalling some 200,000 tonnes, would head from the Middle East between now and next month, "so there should not be a problem of supply shortage".
"Some said there is a shortage, but I don't think so," the major said. "There is no reason for such high prices."
In the swaps market, March paper was last quoted at 103.50/105.00 per tonne, up from $102.00/$103.50 on Friday.
Thailand has yet to award its tender to buy 10,000 tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur grade fuel oil for delivery March 3-7 on Friday.
On Monday, Taiwan tendered to sell 30,000 tonnes of 3.0-percent sulphur oil for loading March 12-28. The tender closes on February 24 and offers are valid for two days.
